Q: html/css canvas width/height handling A:

// Código simples para um jogo em HTML5 Canvas

const canvas = document.getElementById('gameCanvas');

const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');

let playerX = canvas.width / 2;

let playerY = canvas.height / 2;

let handsTogether = true;

let score = 0;

let energyBalls = [];

// Desenhar o menino (simplificado)

function drawPlayer() {

ctx.fillStyle = 'gray';

ctx.fillRect(playerX - 15, playerY - 30, 30, 60); // corpo

ctx.fillStyle = 'brown';

ctx.fillRect(playerX - 10, playerY - 40, 20, 20); // cabeça

if (handsTogether) {

ctx.fillStyle = 'brown';

ctx.fillRect(playerX - 5, playerY - 10, 10, 20); // mãos juntas

}

}

// Gerar bolas de energia

function generateEnergy() {

if (Math.random() < 0.05) {

energyBalls.push({

  x: Math.random() \* canvas.width,

  y: Math.random() \* canvas.height,

  color: \`hsl(${Math.random() \* 360}, 100%, 50%)\`

});

}

}

// Desenhar bolas de energia

function drawEnergy() {

energyBalls.forEach((ball, i) => {

ctx.fillStyle = ball.color;

ctx.beginPath();

ctx.arc(ball.x, ball.y, 10, 0, Math.PI \* 2);

ctx.fill();

if (Math.abs(ball.x - playerX) \< 20 && Math.abs(ball.y - playerY) \< 20 && handsTogether) {

  score++;

  energyBalls.splice(i, 1);

}

});

}

// Controlar o jogo

function gameLoop() {

ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);

drawPlayer();

generateEnergy();

drawEnergy();

ctx.fillStyle = 'black';

ctx.font = '20px Arial';

ctx.fillText('Score: ' + score, 10, 30);

if (!handsTogether) {

ctx.fillText('Você perdeu a concentração!', canvas.width / 2 - 100, canvas.height / 2);

return;

}

requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop);

}

// Simular controle de mãos (exemplo simples)

canvas.addEventListener('click', () => {

handsTogether = !handsTogether;

});

gameLoop();

Q: Geographic plotting A: 
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import matplotlib.lines as mlines
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import geopandas as gpd

points = ["POINT (18.04538 59.32689)", "POINT (18.09599 59.30791)"]
lines = ["LINESTRING (18.02005 59.31730, 18.10860 59.32257)"]
polygons = ["POLYGON ((18.07049 59.31784, 18.06063 59.30690, 18.09853 59.31472, 18.07049 59.31784))"]

point_df = gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=gpd.GeoSeries().from_wkt(data=points, crs=4326))
line_df = gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=gpd.GeoSeries().from_wkt(data=lines, crs=4326))
poly_df = gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=gpd.GeoSeries().from_wkt(data=polygons, crs=4326))

blue_point = mlines.Line2D([], [], color="blue", linewidth=0, markersize=10, marker="o", label="blue point")
red_line = mlines.Line2D([], [], color="red", linewidth=2, label="red line")
green_poly = mpatches.Patch(color="green", label="green polygon")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1,1,figsize=(10, 6))

poly_df.plot(ax=ax, color="green", zorder=1)
line_df.plot(ax=ax, color="red", linewidth=2, zorder=2)
point_df.plot(ax=ax, color="blue", markersize=10, marker="o")
ax.legend(handles = [blue_point, red_line, green_poly])

Q: What is the rationale for having two distinct operators (*args and **kwargs) for arbitrary arguments in Python? A:

Any object collecting all possible arguments would need a sequence-like part, and a mapping-like part - effectively, a tuple, list, or object with two attributes.

That said, it makes sence that a "tuple[tuple, dict]" could be more confortable as a single object - it just was not made this way more than 20 years ago.

But now that you say it, since the vast majority of cases will just forward both args and kwargs unchanged, maybe a third form, representing an object that'd gather both could be used in future versions:

This seens like a straightforward topic to be placed on Python's Ideas discourse group.

I believe a 3-asterix prefix could be a straightforward way to represent a tuple[tuple, dict] whose members would be equivalent to the current args and kwargs.

Q: How to call google sheets current row and have it work with date/time? A:

your 2025-02-06T12:30:00+02:00 is not a valid datetime value. see answer of Locale differences in Google Sheets (documentation missing pages)

use:

=IF(NOW() > SUM(SPLIT(INDIRECT("C" & ROW()), "T+")), "past", "future")
